correctness.rationale: Exact electrical series-parallel reduction gives R=δ(L−δ)/L. Four integrations by parts give strictly negative nonzero Fourier coefficients of R²; the resulting sum-of-squares quadratic form is strictly negative for every nonzero zero-sum coefficient vector, by the zero-to-(m−1)-frequency Vandermonde invertibility. The explicit ℓ² embedding has the correct metric. Exact cyclic Laplacian difference equations yield every unit-cycle Gram eigenvalue; elementary sine/Chebyshev products yield the exact pseudodeterminant and simplex volume, including n=3. A three-vertex Hilbert triangle bound forces the regular-cycle finite exponent upper limit 2; finite strictness at 2 plus compactness gives >2 for each finite sample, while the continuum cannot exceed 2. Standalone source independently checked 12 exact rational weighted resistance matrices, 7 exact simplex determinant cases, Fourier samples n=3..31. Finite checks corroborate, do not replace, universal proof.

originality.rationale: Direct equivalence and implication comparisons were carried out with published mathematical records, the related prior mathematical claims and primary full texts. Classical Schoenberg and resistance formula results are conceded as antecedents. The materially stronger weighted-cycle strict 2-negative type of R itself, exact unit-cycle simplex spectra/volume and finite/continuum boundary were not implied by the inspected statements. One relevant circulant study was abstract-only and the classical Bernoulli/Fourier identity introduces residual priority risk; neither was misrepresented as checked full-text noncoverage.
residual_risks: The exact fourth-degree periodic Bernoulli kernel may have been described elsewhere as an isometric circle embedding; classical Fourier identity itself is not claimed new.
The full text of Zhang–Yang 2006 circulant resistance paper could not be read; its abstract is not evidence of whole-document noncoverage.
Indexing and semantic searches cannot prove novelty, and a stronger specialized negative-type theorem could dominate this result.

value.rationale: The metric R is known as squared Hilbert distance for any network, but its own Euclidean embeddability is a genuinely stronger and generally false property. Characterizing every positive weighted cycle as a full-dimensional Euclidean resistance simplex is a natural structural graph-family result, with exact Fourier map and universal strictness; the sharp 2-exponent continuum/finite distinction and closed-form Gram spectrum and simplex volume provide reusable geometric invariants. A three-leaf star demonstrates meaningful boundary. The work does not assert exact finite supremal exponents, only justified strict lower and useful asymptotically sharp upper bounds.
